premises.statement: A closed opportunity with NULL opportunity_age_days should receive a Long Cycle Win or Long Cycle Loss velocity category.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: when opportunity_age_days<=180 then 'Extended Win (91-180d)' else 'Long Cycle Win (>180d)' end
premises.alternative: The contract defines long-cycle categories as ">180" days, while opportunity_age_days is explicitly nullable when created_date is missing.
premises.reason: Missing durations are classified as known long cycles rather than remaining unclassified.

premises.statement: The manager performance result does not need to be ordered by team_total_bookings_amount descending.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: from manager_rollup r left join staging.stg_salesforce__user u on r.manager_id=u.user_id
premises.alternative: The contract requires "the final result is ordered by team_total_bookings_amount descending".
premises.reason: The omitted ordering affects the explicitly prescribed result presentation but not metric values.

premises.statement: A NULL quarter-over-quarter revenue growth rate should contribute 10 points to the team health score.
premises.alternative: The contract specifies "20 if > 10%, else 15 if > 0%, else 10 if ≥ -10%, else 5" and permits NULL growth when previous-quarter revenue is zero or NULL.
premises.reason: Teams without a measurable growth rate receive five additional health points.

premises.statement: Ordinary equality is sufficient to match performer-name groups when team_type is NULL.
premises.alternative: The contract explicitly says "team_type = user_type (can be null)" and requires performer names for each group.
premises.reason: NULL team types cannot match through the equality join, losing both performer names for affected teams.

premises.statement: A negative previous-quarter revenue total should yield NULL quarter-over-quarter growth.
premises.alternative: The contract specifies growth as the percentage change and says it is "null if previous-quarter revenue is zero or null", not negative.
premises.reason: Negative revenue baselines would suppress a required growth value and alter health scoring.

premises.statement: Closed-opportunity won revenue is the intended ranking measure for top_revenue_performer rather than the user's total_won_amount.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: arg_max(full_name,total_revenue_won) filter(where total_revenue_won is not null)
premises.alternative: The contract specifies "the full_name of the member with the highest total won amount"; member_metrics also selects p.total_won_amount, whose upstream definition counts opportunities marked won without requiring closed status.
premises.reason: The two revenue measures can rank team members differently.

premises.statement: Teams whose members all lack a ranking measure should have no top performer instead of selecting an arbitrary member.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: arg_max(full_name,win_rate_percentage) filter(where win_rate_percentage is not null)
premises.alternative: The contract says "members without a value are ranked last; ties are arbitrary", which supports retaining such members as candidates even when all values are missing.
premises.reason: Filtering missing measures removes every candidate in all-missing teams.

fewer.reason: Most transformations follow explicit contract rules; relevant upstream key-uniqueness premises were already recorded.
The aggregation and enrichment otherwise follow the documented rules, and upstream monetary-type premises were already recorded.
